sentences.text: Luke Miels became chief executive officer of GSK plc and joined its board on 1 January 2026, after being appointed CEO designate in September 2025, succeeding Dame Emma Walmsley.

sentences.quote: Luke joined GSK in 2017 and is currently Chief Commercial Officer, with world-wide responsibility for medicines and vaccines1. He has been instrumental in building GSK's specialty medicines portfolio, notably in oncology and respiratory.
sentences.text: He joined GSK in 2017 as chief commercial officer with worldwide responsibility for medicines and vaccines, and was instrumental in building the company's specialty medicines portfolio, notably in oncology and respiratory.

Before GSK he held senior roles in the United States, Europe and Asia at AstraZeneca, Roche and Sanofi-Aventis, beginning his career in sales and marketing at AstraZeneca and later serving as Roche's regional head for Asia Pacific.
An Australian, he holds a Bachelor of Science in biology from Flinders University, Adelaide, and an MBA from Macquarie University, Sydney.

sentences.quote: Miels will be tasked with leading a new phase for the company and delivering GSK's sales target of more than 40 billion pounds ($53.78 billion) by 2031.
sentences.text: As CEO he is tasked with delivering GSK's target of more than 40 billion pounds of sales by 2031.

sentences.text: GSK's Specialty Medicines arm is the main growth engine, with first-half 2026 sales up 14 per cent at constant currency on double-digit growth in HIV, respiratory/immunology and oncology, and long-acting HIV injectables drove 80 per cent of HIV growth in the second quarter, with year-to-date sales above 1 billion pounds.

On track for 2031 sales outlook of more than GBP 40 billion; Accelerating growth from 2031 onwards
sentences.text: Management guides to 2026 turnover growth of 3 to 5 per cent and core operating profit and core EPS growth of 7 to 9 per cent at constant rates, with a 2031 sales outlook above 40 billion pounds and growth accelerating beyond 2031.
A new three-year "Accelerate Growth" programme funds R&D, and GSK has accelerated assets across 18 indications for seven late-stage products and now plans 20-plus phase III starts in 2026.
Cash returns continue: 70 pence of dividend is expected for 2026 and the 2 billion pound buyback has been completed.
